seo_meta_description: Master Data Analysis on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Table Regression for Linear/Exponential Models
techniques.syntax: y1 ~ mx1 + b or y1 ~ ab^x1
techniques.description: Input data points into a table and use the tilde (~) operator to force Desmos to find the line of best fit or exponential curve.
techniques.when_to_use: When given a set of data points and asked to predict a value or find the equation of the model.
techniques.pro_tip: Always check the R^2 value; if it is 1, the model is a perfect fit.

techniques.title: Mean and Median Calculation
techniques.description: Define a list L = [x1, x2, ...] and use built-in functions to find central tendency instantly.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked to compare means/medians of two datasets or calculate the effect of adding a new data point.
techniques.pro_tip: Use the 'stats' menu in the keypad to quickly insert these functions.

techniques.title: Standard Deviation and Range
techniques.description: Calculates the spread of data instantly without manual formula application.
techniques.when_to_use: When questions ask about the impact of outliers on standard deviation or range.
techniques.pro_tip: Remember that adding a constant to every value in a set does not change the standard deviation.

techniques.title: Scatter Plot Visualization
techniques.description: Plotting points directly to visualize trends, outliers, or correlation direction.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked to describe the relationship between two variables (positive, negative, or no correlation).
techniques.pro_tip: Click the wrench icon to adjust the axes if your points are not visible.

techniques.title: Weighted Average Calculation
techniques.description: Use list multiplication to find weighted averages for frequency tables.
techniques.when_to_use: When given a frequency table and asked for the mean value.
techniques.pro_tip: Define L1 as the values and L2 as the frequencies.

speed_walkthroughs.problem: The table shows the number of hours 5 students studied. What is the mean number of hours studied? Data: {2, 4, 5, 7, 12}

drills.question: A data set has a mean of 10 and a standard deviation of 2. If each value is increased by 5, what is the new standard deviation?
explanation: Step 1: Create a list of numbers.
Step 3: Add 5 to each number in the list and calculate stdev again.
Step 4: Observe that the value remains unchanged.

drills.question: The following data points are given: (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6). If the relationship is linear, what is the value of y when x = 10?
explanation: Step 1: Create a table with the points.
Step 3: Use the resulting m and b to evaluate for x=10.
